About this tool

Full explanation & FAQ

What this tool tells you

Answer a few questions to find out why your damage was low this time or has stopped growing: left-hero choice, troop ratio, overlapping skills, gear and talent progress. You get the most likely causes, what to fix first and how.

How it works

Factors that affect Bear Hunt damage (joiners' first expedition skill, overlapping leader skills, troop ratio, troop tier, stats, pets and buffs) are turned into a checklist, and your answers rank the likely causes by impact. The rules come from public community tests and our own measurements, not from the game's internal formulas.

How to use it

Just answer the questions in order. Once all are answered you see the likely causes, the fixes and links to the matching tools (Left-Hero Checker, Troop Ratio Simulator, etc.). After fixing, estimate the gain in the simulator.

What is the Damage Doctor?

"My Bear Hunt damage was low this time — why?" This unofficial diagnostic narrows down the cause by asking you a few questions: left-hero mistakes, troop ratio, rally-leader choice, rotation, exclusive gear and more — then shows the likely cause and a concrete fix.

How to use it

  1. Answer the questions (yes / no, etc.).
  2. Based on your answers, the most likely causes are narrowed down.
  3. You get a fix for each cause, with links to the relevant tools and guides.

Common causes it surfaces

  • Left-hero (rally leader) mistake: the 1st expedition skill isn't rally-suited. → check with the Left-Hero Checker.
  • Mismatched troop ratio: e.g. all-marksman with a thin front line. → compare in the Troop Ratio Simulator.
  • Rally leadership / timing: too few rallies or a weak rally organizer.
  • Gear / talents not built: the upside is on the gear side.

Once you find the cause, re-test the improved setup in the Bear Hunt Damage Simulator to confirm the gain.

FAQ

Will the diagnosis always be right?
It's there to help narrow things down. Causes can stack, so try the suggested fixes one by one.
Can beginners use it?
Yes. Just answer the questions — no jargon required. Terms are explained in the guides.
